name: Wasl adversarial robustness matrix
evidence_scope: Built controls plus executed hermetic and real single-node NATS tests. This is not production-readiness evidence.

environment.nats_test_wiring: Temporary worktree-local bin/nats-server symlink to the system binary; not a source change.
environment.fuzz: Native Go fuzzing, four workers, three seconds per target for the recorded smoke run. Raw per-target logs are retained under evidence/adversarial-fuzz-2026-11-09/; baseline-only or zero-generation passes are rejected.
environment.filesystem: Local macOS filesystem. Write, short-write, sync, close and missing-parent faults are injected in process; physical ENOSPC and power loss were not injected.

seed_policy.deterministic_tests: Checked-in table fixtures and fixed message IDs; no wall-clock-dependent expected hashes.
seed_policy.fuzz: Checked-in seed corpora plus the Go fuzz engine and its persistent coverage cache. The Go tool does not expose a numeric fuzz-engine seed flag, so exact generated sequences are not claimed reproducible. Duration and invariants are reproducible; any failure artifact must be added as a deterministic regression.

seeds: explicit duplicate outer resourceType and nested sign-off keys in deterministic and fuzz-seed fixtures
cases.evidence: The deterministic test and FuzzNormaliseNeverPanics seed corpus both execute explicit outer and nested duplicate fixtures. Malformed shapes return no Event/Signoff and do not panic; duplicate JSON keys are rejected. Generated fuzz executions are recorded separately in native-fuzz-smoke.
cases.limitations: Clinical semantic validation is not complete; see unresolved findings.

seeds: null embedded Patient with and without PID
cases.evidence: Invalid segments/resources return errors without panics; ToResource rejects embedded resources that normalise drops; bounded framing rejects oversize input.
cases.limitations: No network slow-client or connection-exhaustion matrix was run.

cases.category: Subscription malformed, duplicate and out-of-order input
cases.evidence: One ordered dispatch per event, duplicate envelope keys and malformed or shape-confused hooks receive 400 without durable acceptance, focus/source mismatches are rejected, a full bounded JetStream inbox receives 503, and unknown sources do not advance acknowledgement.
cases.limitations: Durable acceptance and overflow replay are covered by the subscription-durable-ack-replay follow-up; remaining process-kill and multi-node limits are listed in its report.

cases.category: FHIR notification durable acceptance, restart and replay
seeds: missing durable inbox then exact sender retry
same event number under sub-a/p1 and sub-b/p2 with restart and gap-fill
concurrent ownership transfer, conflicting-writer overwrite attempt, and stale deletion attempt
startup status failure with recovered event 2 pending and with checkpoint-only state
mismatched status and events response identities
legacy checkpoint binding, scoped/legacy subscription isolation, legacy-overflow exact retry, and monotonic migration
conflicting duplicate event entries in one notification
malformed, empty and invalid-status HTTP 200 retry
canonical publish before inbox ack with genuine consumer replacement
restart after pending write before inbox ack
cases.evidence: Fifty-four direct durable/FHIR-hook test/subtest outcomes pass across 40 explicit top-level tests with a real single-node NATS server. SetupStreamsCreatesBoundedDurableInbox, StatusRejectsMismatchedSubscription, and UnknownSubscriptionSourceDoesNotAdvanceAcknowledgement are explicitly selected and pass in both direct and combined race JSON; broad-prefix-only unrelated tests are excluded. The combined clinical/durable race lane has 280 passes across 71 top-level tests. HTTP 200 follows JetStream acceptance, retries have one logical effect, pending storage precedes inbox acknowledgement, provider/subscription/event identity survives restart and gap-fill, CAS ownership blocks stale deletion, and startup status failure leaves gap recovery scheduled.
cases.limitations: Synthetic in-process consumer replacement and explicit ack boundaries, not an OS process-kill matrix. No injected publish timeout, multi-node partition, physical media fault, Malaffi feed, external exactly-once, or production claim. See evidence/fhir-durable-ack-replay-2026-11-10.md.

cases.category: Clinical timestamp, programme and DiagnosticReport status normalization
seeds: missing/malformed timestamps on all seven clinical resource types and HL7 non-report conversions
YYYY, YYYY-MM and YYYY-MM-DD partial forms
unknown ServiceRequest, Appointment and DiagnosticReport programme mappings
all ten FHIR R4 DiagnosticReport statuses
v1 adequate human sign-off followed by corrected v2 inadequate/disagreeing/unavailable readers
forged v2 sign-off item identity and legacy v0/v1 replay
versioned prep replies and automatic-v2 provenance
same-body/different-ID correction and withdrawal in both arrival orders
equal-key early break, higher/equal-version conflicts and empty-body ownership
generic/DR/lung omitted TX, conclusion fallback and coded OBX
live versus materialized PREP and embedded-body replay
cases.evidence: Two hundred twenty-six focused test/subtest outcomes pass across 31 explicit top-level tests. Structured PREP rejection codes replace day-0 and unknown-programme defaults. Only current final/amended/corrected/appended reports produce downstream evidence facts; cancellations and entered-in-error versions withdraw prior facts. Human overrides/reviews and prep replies are report-version bound with legacy v0/v1 compatibility, v2+ item identity checks, append-only sign-offs and version-correct provenance. A normalized-body newest-version barrier preserves correction/withdrawal precedence in both arrival orders and cleans empty-body ownership. HL7 identities reconcile before publishable output, omitted OBX clears generic/DR/lung embedded content and conclusion fallback, generic CE/CWE uses the first component, and non-report HL7 time rejection/embedded replay matches direct FHIR. The explicit combined race lane has 280 passes across 71 top-level tests; the full suite has 1,505 passes, 8 intentional skips and no failures. Final cumulative independent review reported no remaining Critical or Important findings.
cases.limitations: Focused synthetic evidence only. Real-feed mappings, report truth, clinician agreement, reader accuracy, clinical effectiveness and production behavior are not established. HL7 identity checks stop at ToResource before the existing listener publish/ACK, not a socket-level durable-stream test. Non-report HL7 time equivalence uses ZWS-2 embedded bodies; segment-only/wiped-ZWS time reconstruction is unsupported. See evidence/fhir-clinical-normalization-2026-11-10.md.

seeds: JSON null, array, string, number, boolean, empty-object and null-output manifests
cases.evidence: Poll/export errors are counted, success/EOF completion is blocked, scanner errors are checked, and test fixtures do not panic. Seven real-NATS regressions prove null, every tested non-object manifest, an empty object, and a null output array leave no success count, checkpoint, resource record, EOF state, or FHIR stream message.
cases.limitations: A valid prefix may already have been published before a later page/line fails; retry relies on dedupe and no completion checkpoint is advanced.

seeds: valid JSON prefix followed by whitespace beyond route limit
cases.evidence: Review, consent and undo use bounded strict decoding and return 400 without appending, including for case variants that Go's typed decoder would otherwise match to one field.

cases.category: CI-bounded parser and API fuzz smoke
cases.evidence: All five targets passed with raw logs in evidence/adversarial-fuzz-2026-11-09/. The runner rejects baseline-only or zero-generation passes. Exact baseline, total, and generated execution counts are recorded in the source-bound verification manifest rather than copied into this matrix.
cases.limitations: Execution counts depend on host/cache and are evidence for this run only, not a coverage guarantee. Logs preserve the exact reported baseline and total counts.

cases.evidence: Command is published; the bounded three-second variant was executed.
cases.limitations: No long-duration or distributed fuzzing claim.

seeds: Two independent apiServer values sharing one run
cases.evidence: One same-head writer wins; the reloaded hash chain remains valid with one event.
cases.limitations: The two-server fixture runs in one OS process with independent open file descriptions. No cross-host/shared-filesystem test was run; flock is Unix-specific.

seeds: terminated and unterminated records over 16 MiB
cases.evidence: Writes are refused or reader becomes unavailable; unsafe replay is not accepted. Bounded fragment reads reject oversized records before whole-record allocation.
cases.limitations: Whole-reader-ledger quarantine is deliberately fail-stop and reduces availability until remediated.

cases.evidence: No in-memory success is acknowledged before durable append; indeterminate ledger state blocks later writers.
cases.limitations: These are hermetic error injections, not physical ENOSPC, filesystem corruption or power-failure tests. Status/materialization/dump paths still have unchecked I/O errors.

seeds: same-id stored twice after 100 ms dedupe window
abrupt broker kill after sequence 1 acknowledgement
cases.evidence: Duplicate-ID scan terminates; acknowledged output survives broker restart; replay does not add a stored effect; existing duplicate/restart cases pass with nats-server v2.15.2.
cases.limitations: Single node and one replica for these tests. No R3 quorum, multi-node partition, network partition or external shared-cluster ownership matrix was run.

cases.command: go -C pipeline test ./... -count=1 -timeout=10m -json && go -C pipeline vet ./...
cases.evidence: The final repaired-source full suite, focused race suite, and vet passed. Raw JSON events are retained in evidence/full-regression-2026-11-09.jsonl. Exact event counts, skips, elapsed time, log hashes, matrix hash, final code-only commit/tree, and deterministic source-only tree are recorded in evidence/verification-2026-11-09.manifest.json.
cases.limitations: Six asset-dependent tests skipped in the final run: TestAPIBookingSupport, TestAPIDRFixtureRun, TestAPIFixturesAndContracts, TestAPIReviewRBACAndAppendOnly, TestFresh2Reader, TestHL7RoundTripCohort.

seeds: five crash windows x reuse off/on
short-write, sync and close ledger faults
conflicting FHIR sign-off and conflicting ledger
cases.evidence: Built and tested for the bounded synthetic single-node matrix only: each crash window is compared with an uninterrupted control for one logical sign-off per item, identical worklists, status, exact ledger hash and stored record; conflicts stop without ACK or publish. Passed three times (316.0s), then full package (275.3s) and go vet. See evidence/reviewer-durable-restart-2026-11-10.md.
cases.limitations: Exactly-once external effects, physical power loss, cross-host locking and clinician performance remain unproven. The failed 24-hour soak limitation is preserved; no soak, normalization or AMD64 run was made.

cases.category: Physical disk-full, torn writes and power loss
cases.command: not published: requires an isolated block device or fault-injection filesystem and a power-failure harness
cases.evidence: Only hermetic filesystem errors and real abrupt process/broker kills were executed.
cases.limitations: No physical media, filesystem or machine-power durability claim.

unresolved_findings: HL7 MLLP remains unauthenticated and EOF control is not separately authorized. Subnet isolation is still required; transport authentication and actor identity are not implemented here.
Sign-off roles/read attestations are payload assertions, not authenticated identities. Effect/kind consistency and dual-review identity binding remain outside this robustness change.
MLLP read sizes are bounded, but per-connection deadlines, connection caps and slow-client network tests are not implemented.

Clinical normalization proposal #2 and its revision/HL7 follow-up are covered by focused synthetic fixtures; real Malaffi mappings, report truth, clinician agreement, reader accuracy and clinical effectiveness remain unverified. HL7 identity coverage stops at ToResource before listener publish/ACK; non-report segment-only time reconstruction is unsupported.

Durable FHIR acceptance/replay is tested only on a synthetic single node; OS-process kill, broker-accepted publish with lost acknowledgement, multi-node partitions, and post-dedupe-window time travel remain unresolved.

Reviewer restart is covered only by a bounded synthetic single-node matrix; exactly-once external effects, physical power loss, cross-host locking and clinician performance remain unproven, and the failed 24-hour soak limitation stands.
writeStatus, materialization and stream-dump I/O errors are not comprehensively propagated; hermetic ledger append tests do not cover those paths.
Malformed PREP/FACTS payloads do not yet have a durable dead-letter contract, and buffered FACTS FSeq provenance can inherit the draining message's sequence.
Fresh setup destructively resets global external NATS streams; active-run namespacing/ownership is not implemented.
The new ledger lock uses Unix flock semantics; Windows and network-filesystem behavior were not verified.
